# Noodles.gl

> A node-based editor for animated maps and geospatial data visualizations, running entirely in the browser on DuckDB-Wasm and deck.gl

## Overview

Noodles.gl is a node-based editor for geospatial visualizations and animations. A project is a document of nodes and edges that Noodles compiles to queries and runs in DuckDB in the browser, so a slider or the timeline re-runs only what a change needs.

Key Features:
- A node graph, a layers list and a properties panel, arranged in workspaces
- The whole graph runs in DuckDB-Wasm; per-row values are columns made by expressions
- Layers drawn with deck.gl over a MapLibre basemap
- A keyframe timeline for any number parameter
- CSV, JSON, Parquet, GeoJSON, GeoParquet, shapefiles and SQL queries
- Export to MP4 video and PNG images

## Use with an AI agent

- Overview of the ways to use Noodles.gl with an agent (in-app assistant, driving a running editor, writing project files): https://noodles.gl/users/ai-agents
- Quick start prompt for Claude Code: https://noodles.gl/claude-code-prompt.txt. It clones the repo, installs, starts the editor, registers the WebMCP relay, changes an example map, and shows a screenshot.
- Quick start prompt for other agents (Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, VS Code, any MCP client): https://noodles.gl/agent-prompt.txt. Same steps, with one restart after the relay is registered.
- Driving a running editor: the `noodles-live` skill at https://github.com/joby-aviation/noodles.gl/blob/main/.claude/skills/noodles-live/SKILL.md
- Writing and validating noodles.json without a browser: the `noodles` MCP server at https://github.com/joby-aviation/noodles.gl/blob/main/noodles-mcp/README.md and the validator at https://github.com/joby-aviation/noodles.gl/blob/main/noodles-validate/README.md
- JSON Schema for noodles.json (file shape only; the validator checks operators and connections): https://noodles.gl/schema/noodles-project.schema.json, with a copy per version at https://noodles.gl/schema/noodles-document.v<N>.schema.json (projects saved before documents: https://noodles.gl/schema/noodles-project.v20.schema.json)
- WebMCP setup and tool list: https://github.com/joby-aviation/noodles.gl/blob/main/dev-docs/claude-code-workflow.md

## Repository Structure

```
/packages/planner/        # Operators, the document format, lowering and the query planner
/noodles-editor/          # The editor (React + TypeScript)
  /src/editor/            # Network, properties panel, layers, workspaces, project files
  /src/runtime/           # Engine, DuckDB worker, deck operators, host operators
  /src/runtime/migrate/   # Converting older operator-graph projects to documents
  /src/noodles/           # Field widgets and the remaining host operator classes
  /src/examples/          # Example projects
/noodles-mcp/             # MCP server: operator schemas, docs, examples, validation
/noodles-validate/        # Project file validator and the operator registry
/docs/                    # Documentation markdown (served by the website)
/website/                 # Documentation site (Docusaurus)
/dev-docs/                # Development and architecture documentation
```

## Technology Stack

### Core Technologies
- **React** - UI framework
- **TypeScript** - Type-safe JavaScript
- **DuckDB-Wasm** - Runs the compiled graph in a worker
- **Deck.gl** - WebGL-powered geospatial visualization
- **MapLibre GL JS** - Map rendering
- **Vite** - Build tool and development server

### Key Libraries
- **Zustand** - State management
- **React Flow** - Node-based editor UI
- **Apache Arrow** - Moves rows and layer buffers out of DuckDB

### Development Setup

```bash
# Install dependencies (npm workspaces)
npm ci

# Start the editor
cd noodles-editor && npm start

# Build the editor and the website, from the repo root
cd .. && npm run build:all
```

### Testing
- Unit tests with Vitest
- Integration tests with Playwright
- Tests co-located with source files (*.test.ts)

## Use Cases

- **Visualization Experts**: Create high-quality, presentation-ready graphics
- **Developers**: Rapid visualization prototyping
- **Data Scientists**: Data exploration and analysis
- **Research Teams**: Publishing polished geospatial analysis and insights

## Architecture

- A project is an `EditorDoc`: nodes (`op`, `name`, `params`) joined by edges between ports.
- `@noodles.gl/planner` lowers the document to relations, attribute expressions and layers, and decides how each parameter is applied: a deck prop, a uniform, a CPU pass, a requery or a rematerialize. A value change never recompiles.
- The engine worker runs the relations in DuckDB-Wasm and hands deck.gl binary attribute buffers.
- A few operators that can't compile (code that reads `op()` or the timeline, geocoding, directions, charts, tiles) run on the main thread as host operators.
- Subnets group nodes; a node's path is its name under its subnets' names (`/subnet/filter`).
- Any number parameter can be keyframed on the timeline.
